Share network diagram and VPC peering guide for Redwood Private
Schedule follow-up to review RBAC model and demo Dedicated setup (propose Jan 6)
Run short pilot on Dedicated nodes with sampled dataset - Redwood to propose pilot scope and cost
action_items: Maya Patel - email SOC2 / ISO artifacts and trust center link by 2027-01-02
Ethan Liu - prepare initial network/VPC handbook and pilot runbook by 2027-01-04
Janelle Park - provide list of compliance questions and retention policy requirements by 2027-01-05
Luis Moreno - share current cloud KMS provider and key rotation cadence by 2027-01-05
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
summary: Discovery call focused on Aquila's security posture and whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated or Private fits their regulatory and data residency needs. Main concerns: SOC 2 / ISO attestations, SSO with SAML and SCIM, RBAC granularity, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS integration and key ownership, and options for Dedicated or Private deployment for PHI-like data. Agreed next steps: send security docs, share network + pilot runbook, schedule RBAC deep-dive and demo.
transcript:
00:00 Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood. Ethan's with me, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:05 Samantha Greene: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to chat.
00:08 Dr. Tomas Alvarez: Hi all. We got the calendar note, this is Tomas, CTO.
00:12 Janelle Park: Janelle here, security. I'll drive most of the questions.
00:15 Ethan Liu: Awesome. Quick agenda: we'll ask about your current stack and reqs, run through our compliance posture (SOC2/ISO), SSO and RBAC, encryption/KMS options, and then talk deployment modes — hosted, dedicated, private — and next steps. Sound good?
00:27 Janelle Park: Yep. We'll mostly focus on compliance and data separation. We handle de-identified clinical data but still want strict controls.
00:33 Maya Patel: Totally. Tomas, can you give quick context on regulatory constraints and timeline?
00:38 Dr. Tomas Alvarez: Sure. We're evaluating vendors now, timeline about Q1 procurement. Main constraints: SOC 2 Type II attestation mandatory, ISO 27001 preferred, SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning, audit logs with 1 year retention (some logs 3 years), and ability to manage keys or use our KMS for encryption at rest. Also, we prefer dedicated tenancy for certain workloads or on-prem for specific customers.
01:02 Samantha Greene: We currently use CloudVendorX and have a separate VPC per environment. We want low-latency inference for a clinician-facing app, but cost matters.
01:12 Ethan Liu: Great. On SOC2/ISO — Redwood has SOC2 Type II completed (link to trust center). We also have ISO 27001 in progress, we can share latest certs and scope. For Hosted API customers we provide SOC2 artifacts and our security whitepaper, for Dedicated we can add contractual controls and tighter network isolation, Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you customer-managed control plane.
01:38 Janelle Park: When you say "customer-managed control plane" for Private, does that mean we bring our own KMS and keys?
01:44 Ethan Liu: Yes, with Redwood Private you can integrate your KMS — we support common KMS providers and HSM integrations. Keys can remain in your account/HSM; Redwood will accept encrypted models/data. There are options for Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) and Customer-Managed Keys.
01:58 Luis Moreno: Which KMS providers are supported? We use Google Cloud KMS for most keys.
02:02 Ethan Liu: We support GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and HSM partners for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can also use envelope encryption — we manage keys but can offer dedicated KMS project options for higher trust.
02:16 Janelle Park: Audit logging — what level of logs do you capture? We need console access logs, API call detail, admin actions, and model audit trails (who invoked which model, prompt/response hashes).
02:26 Maya Patel: We capture API request metadata, admin console events, and model invocation logs. For Hosted we provide logs via our console and can stream them to your SIEM via secure syslog or cloud storage. For Dedicated/Private we can forward logs directly to your logging account. Retention configurable, default 90 days but extendable to 1 year+ with add-on.
02:45 Janelle Park: Is the log stream tamper-evident? We need immutability for certain records.
02:49 Ethan Liu: For Dedicated/Private deployments we support write-once storage options and can enable signed audit records. We also integrate with immutability features in customer's cloud logging (e.g., object lock). We'll include details in the trust center doc.
02:59 Samantha Greene: On SSO, we use Okta; need SAML2 SSO + SCIM provisioning to auto-provision service accounts and roles. How granular is Redwood's RBAC?
03:10 Ethan Liu: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with fine-grained permissions at route/model and org/project level. You can create custom roles for auditing, invoke-only, admin, billing, etc. For Dedicated/Private we can add IP whitelists and network-level restrictions.
03:28 Janelle Park: Does RBAC cover access to logs and audit trails?
03:31 Maya Patel: Yes — logs and audit access are controlled by role. We can map to your groups via SCIM.
03:35 Dr. Tomas Alvarez: Data residency — some customers insist data stays in EU. How do you handle region pinning?
03:40 Ethan Liu: We have regionally deployed clusters and you can pin workloads to region, and for Private you can run on-prem or in your cloud region. Hosted is available in multiple regions; we'll share region coverage.
03:52 Luis Moreno: For the clinician app, latency is critical. Any benchmarks for p99 latency on hosted vs dedicated?
03:57 Ethan Liu: We have benchmark sheets. Hosted optimized for general low-latency; Dedicated gives predictable p99 with reserved throughput; Private/on-prem yields lowest unpredictable latency but requires ops. We'll share a benchmark spreadsheet.
04:10 Janelle Park: Encryption at rest — if we use Hosted, do you manage the keys? If so, what's the contract/control? We prefer BYOK for PHI.
04:18 Maya Patel: For Hosted we by default manage keys, but we offer an enterprise option with customer-dedicated KMS project or BYOK with HSM integration. We'll surface contractual terms for key custody in the security docs.
04:28 Samantha Greene: Retention: we want some artifacts (prompts/outputs) deleted after 30 days for certain flows. Is selective retention possible?
04:34 Ethan Liu: Yes — we support per-route retention policies and can configure zero retention for sensitive routes. For Hosted we provide configurable retention rules and can set auto-delete. For Dedicated/Private you control retention directly.
04:48 Janelle Park: Any penetration testing or VAPT reports we can see?
04:51 Maya Patel: We run regular pentests and can share executive summaries and remediation status; full reports require an NDA.
04:58 Dr. Tomas Alvarez: One more — incident response SLA and notification windows?
05:02 Maya Patel: We have incident response commitments with notification timelines depending on severity. We'll include our IR runbook excerpt in the packet.
05:08 Samantha Greene: Cost question — Dedicated sounds great, but how does pricing compare? We need ballpark for a pilot.
05:13 Ethan Liu: We'll propose a pilot cost for Dedicated reserved nodes for 30 days with metrics collection; it's usually higher per-hour but more predictable and you get isolation. We'll include options for burst capacity and autoscale.
05:25 Janelle Park: Can you do a short demo of the admin console and RBAC after you send docs?
05:29 Maya Patel: Absolutely — we'll schedule a demo. Proposed Jan 6 for RBAC demo and pilot scope review.
05:35 Luis Moreno: We'll need a network diagram and sample terraform for VPC peering if Private.
05:39 Ethan Liu: We'll include a network/VPC handbook and sample Terraform in the follow-up. Link placeholders: trust center - https://redwood.ai/trust (shared), pilot runbook doc (to be sent).
05:50 Maya Patel: Great. Any final questions?
05:53 Janelle Park: Nothing else from me.
05:55 Dr. Tomas Alvarez: No, that's it. Thanks.
05:58 Maya Patel: Thanks everyone — recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, IR runbook excerpt, network/VPC guide, benchmark spreadsheet, and propose pilot scope and cost. Schedule RBAC demo for Jan 6. Action items as noted.
06:08 Samantha Greene: Thanks all.
06:10 End of recording

Notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-heard terms (e.g., "K V cache" for KV cache, "Redwood Private" sometimes transcribed as "Redwood privatee"). Shared artifacts referenced but not embedded: trust center link, pilot runbook, benchmark spreadsheet, network handbook.
